items.actClause: AN ACT to amend chapter 396 of the laws of 2010 amending the alcoholic beverage control law relating to liquidator's permits and temporary retail permits, in relation to the effectiveness of certain provisions thereof
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5261

TITLE OF BILL:

An act
to amend chapter 396 of the laws of 2010 amending the alcoholic beverage
control law relating to liquidator's permits and temporary retail
permits, in relation to the effectiveness of certain provisions thereof

PURPOSE:

To extend for two additional years the temporary retail permit system
within New York state's Alcoholic Beverage control law.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

This bill would amend chapter 396 of the laws of 2010 to extend for
two additional years, the provisions of the alcoholic beverage
control law which authorized the state liquor authority to issue
temporary retail and liquidation permits.

Without this bill, such authorization would expire and be deemed
repealed on August 3, 2011.

JUSTIFICATION:

This legislation would continue the authorization of the state liquor
authority to issue temporary retail permits to help businesses
that are just starting and normally would have to wait for the
Authority's extremely long backlog. This highly successful program
has helped to promote economic growth, and the collection of tax
revenue by having the business up and running with the local and
state economy benefitting from the increased economic activity.

This bill also ensure that a licensee could not continue to obtain a
liquidation permit, which would allow the licensee to sell its entire
stock of alcoholic beverages to other licensees, if the former is
considered delinquent under the provisions of section 101-aa or
section 101-aaa of NYS Alcoholic Beverage law.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None noted.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

60th day after becoming law.

summary: Relates to the effectiveness of provisions of the alcoholic beverage control law relating to temporary retail permits; provides that such provisions expire on October 12, 2012.
